greeting.text: I am Kiato, of the Seabed Temple. The dance is my prayer and my blade. You may call me by name.
You walk with purpose. Good. The dance begins with the first step, and so does every journey.
Forgive my sister if she talks your ear off. She means well. ...Usually.
Your deeds are known even to the Sea God's servants. I am honoured to meet you, {player}.

hint.text: The dance teaches one thing: be where the blow is not. It sounds simple. It takes a lifetime.
A body that moves without fear is harder to strike. Fear tightens; the dance releases.
When a missile comes, turn it. When a blow comes, step out. When both come, dance.
If you carry the Butoh book, the dance wakes by itself: the body learns to slip out of a blow. Mine is only more practised.
My grandfather is the High Priest of the Temple. He taught me that tradition is a river, not a wall.
The surface is brighter than I imagined. Kahono sings to the sky every evening. I pretend not to listen.
Do not fight the rhythm of a boss. Learn it, and step between its beats.
No champions defeated. Begin with patience. Watch the first guardian dance before you join it.
The Eye of the Midnight Sun came to our temple once. I will say no more. Defeat them, and the sea grows calmer.
Vetto is gone. My sister and I owe you a debt we cannot repay in words.
The Spade Kingdom's gravity is a heavy dance. Learn its rhythm, then move where it is not.
Lucius reads a fight like a score. Change the tempo.
Other worlds have other dances. I would like to learn from their warriors, if they will teach.

farewell.text: May the sea carry your steps.
